clue.text: Show contempt for blokes, say, and hide

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for treating them with contempt

indicators.note: say signals that the word for blokes is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: blokes are guys, men

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the men around them and then goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns GUYS into its sound-alike GUISE, a word for an outward appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To disguise something is to conceal it under a false appearance, so it can mean hide.

clue.text: Who perhaps has erected fake Dartmoor landmark?

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down entry the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: cod means fake, as in a cod accent
a tor is a rocky hill, typical of Dartmoor in Devon

explanation.surface: Someone has put up a fake monument on Dartmoor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns COD upwards to DOC. Dartmoor is a moorland in south-west England dotted with rocky hills called tors.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who is the long-running British TV series, so the Doctor is an example of Who.

clue.text: Old coin and old gong seen in part of palace

parts.note: a stater was an ancient Greek coin
a gong is slang for a medal or honour; OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: An old coin and a medal are on display in the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or honour; OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateroom is a grand room for ceremonial occasions in a palace.

clue.text: Be haughty towards university servant crossing street

indicators.note: crossing says the servant word spans across the street abbreviation, holding it

parts.note: a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A college servant gets snooty as they cross the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to treat them snobbishly or outshine them, behaving haughtily towards them.

clue.text: Hospital getting cross about support being only temporary?

indicators.note: about says the annoyed word goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: sore means cross, annoyed
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital is angry that its financial support is only short term.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by description: a shore is a prop put up for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A shore is a beam propping up a wall or ship, usually a temporary brace.

clue.text: Plough missing big bird

indicators.note: missing tells us the word for big is dropped from the star group's name

parts.note: the Plough is the British name for the star group Americans call the Big Dipper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large bird has gone missing from a ploughed field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plough' looks like farming, but it is the constellation, called the Big Dipper in America; 'missing big' strips BIG away.
explanation.definitionFit: The dipper is a small songbird of fast streams that bobs and dives underwater for food.

clue.text: Is the man left without old woman an outcast?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the man's word surrounds the mother

parts.note: the man is he
old woman is slang for mother, ma

explanation.surface: Is a man left without his mother a social outcast?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. Ishmael, son of Abraham, was cast out into the wilderness in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael, driven out in the Bible, became a byword for an outcast.

clue.text: Dull person, quiet and old-fashioned character

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction meaning quiet
a rune is a letter of an ancient alphabet

explanation.surface: A boring, quiet old-fashioned type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter, not a person, here.
explanation.definitionFit: Prune is informal for a dull, prim or disagreeable person.

clue.text: One gent involved with radiatior originally

definitions.text: One gent involved with radiatior originally

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word
involved means twisted up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A gentleman pioneer of radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes the first two words. Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays, and the roentgen is a unit of radiation, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Roentgen was the physicist who discovered X-rays, a man tied up with radiation.

clue.text: Academic boss taking notes for financial purposes

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob on a surface
IOUs are written notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A university head takes notes for money matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager, but it is a raised knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious and academic both describe someone devoted to study.

clue.text: He throws out cash freely to construct a mansion

indicators.note: freely says the letters of the fodder are thrown about loosely into a new order

explanation.surface: A rich man flings his money about to build himself a grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges HE THROWS OUT CASH. CHATSWORTH HOUSE is the Duke of Devonshire's stately home in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatsworth House is a famous English stately home, an example of a mansion.

clue.text: Run round gym at speed

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
PE is physical education, the school gym lesson
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A jogger does laps of the gym at a good pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' reads as jogging, but it is the definition in the sense of running a machine or a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine or business is to run it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Face needs "twitchy therapy" in a manner of speaking

parts.note: dial is slang for a face, also the face of a clock
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, sets the body twitching

explanation.surface: A nervous face needs some treatment to calm the twitching.
explanation.walkthrough: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric-shock treatment that makes the patient twitch; the quotation marks flag a cryptic description.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, a particular manner of speaking.

clue.text: Youngster without restriction, with nothing censured

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the child's word goes around the restraint

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a rein is a restriction, as in keeping a rein on spending
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A child running wild with nothing holding them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear into someone is to attack them verbally, so tore into means censured.

clue.text: This undistinguished band must be bad

definitions.text: This undistinguished band must be bad

parts.words: This undistinguished band must be bad
parts.note: a group without any reputation or title is one nobody has heard of, perhaps because it is no good

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on an unknown band.
explanation.definitionFit: Nameless means having no name or fame, so undistinguished and obscure.

clue.text: Hire facility requires initial deposit of pound

indicators.note: an initial deposit is paid first, so the pound sign is put at the front

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: A rental business asks for a pound up front as a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hire facility' looks like one phrase for a rental shop, but only 'Hire' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease something is to rent it, a straight synonym for hire.

clue.text: Besotted pair hated enforced separation

indicators.note: besotted means fuddled or drunk, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A love-struck couple loathed being kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Besotted' rearranges PAIR HATED; apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was the policy of enforced racial separation in South Africa.

clue.text: Flower people at work in a jolly party

parts.note: a flower is a river, something that flows; the Fal is a river in Cornwall
staff are the people employed at a workplace

explanation.surface: Flower-power people having a merry time at a work party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows, a river: the Fal in Cornwall, south-west England. 'party' means a person, as in a third party.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, merry knight, so a jolly person.

clue.text: Help this person brought in, being trained

indicators.note: brought in says one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: aid means help
this person is the setter speaking of themself, me

explanation.surface: A trainee is helped by being brought into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is the crossword setter's way of saying ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun trained on a target is pointed at it, which is what aimed means.

clue.text: After end of year more than one worker moves elsewhere

indicators.note: after says the workers come behind the month

parts.note: December, Dec, is the last month of the year
worker ants are the workers of a colony

explanation.surface: When the year ends, several workers relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the ant, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant is to move people out to other accommodation, so decants means moves elsewhere.

clue.text: Something in large type, like the notice by motorway

indicators.note: by means beside, so the motorway letter stands next to the rest

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
as means like
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A big roadside sign next to the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is a newspaper's title printed in big letters across the front page.

clue.text: Bob possibly finds atmosphere cold in shed

indicators.note: in places the atmosphere and cold inside the shed

parts.note: a hut is a shed
air is the atmosphere
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Bob finds the air in the garden shed chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name, but it is a short hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short hairstyle, one example of a haircut.

clue.text: Preamble? It's most important that should be short

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: leading means most important, foremost

explanation.surface: A warning that the key thing is to keep it brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is an introduction to something, so a kind of preamble.

clue.text: Patient? Woman keeps one in bed after setback

indicators.note: keeps says the woman's name holds the rest inside it

parts.note: Sal is a woman's name, short for Sally

indicators.note: in says the figure one goes inside the bed
after setback means the bed word is turned backwards

parts.note: a cot is a bed
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A patient woman lies in bed recovering after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after setback' turns the bed word backwards (TOC) and 'in' puts the numeral into it, giving TOIC before the woman's name wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stoical bears trouble without complaint, which is being patient.

clue.text: Old characters turn up and play without permit

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: without says the permit word is taken away

parts.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's play
let means permit

explanation.surface: Old letters turn up, and a play goes on without a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GO into OG; 'without' removes LET from HAMLET. Ogham is an ancient Irish alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an alphabet used in early Irish inscriptions, so its letters are old characters.

clue.text: Exciting drink purifier gets a mention

indicators.note: gets a mention says the word is spoken, so we want its sound-alike

parts.note: a filter purifies water or air

explanation.surface: A water purifier is talked up as making an exciting drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A philtre is a love potion, a drink meant to arouse desire.

clue.text: Drama on a piece of land liable to flood

definitions.text: piece of land liable to flood

parts.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A drama is staged on a stretch of floodplain.
explanation.definitionFit: A playa is a desert basin that floods to a shallow lake after rain.

clue.text: The Canadians are unorthodox in Christian doctrine

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Canadians hold irregular beliefs within Christianity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges all three opening words; the Athanasian Creed is a statement of Christian belief about the Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athanasian Creed is a statement of faith used in Christian churches, an example of doctrine.

clue.text: Bleak for one having to eat American or starve

indicators.note: having to eat says the fish word takes the other inside it

parts.note: the bleak is a small freshwater fish

explanation.surface: In bleak times, one has to eat American food or go hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bleak' looks like an adjective, but it is a small river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is an old verb meaning to starve or make extremely hungry.

clue.text: Huge animal could spell ant's doom

indicators.note: could spell suggests the letters can be arranged to spell something else

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters a, n, t, s

explanation.surface: A giant beast might mean the end for a tiny ant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could spell' reads as 'could mean', but it rearranges the letters of ANT'S DOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastodon was a huge extinct elephant-like mammal.
